sourceArticle.title: These Git Repositories Changed How I Manage My Home Lab
sourceArticle.author: Brandon Lee

athenaOutput.directive: Transform the Home Lab from a passive hardware collection into a Sovereign, Agent-Managed Autonomous Zone driven entirely by self-hosted Forgejo GitOps.
athenaOutput.rationale: To achieve true Artist Liberation and enforce the NAS Supremacy Rule, the home lab's infrastructure must be defined, versioned, and executed through an immutable Git pipeline. Repositories are no longer just code storage; they are the active, living contracts that the Creative Liberation Engine agents read, write, and execute to maintain the system's sovereignty, eliminating manual workstation administration.

options.title: The Sovereign GitOps Spine (Infrastructure as Code)
options.description: Centralize all NAS Docker configurations, network routing, and system contracts into a master Forgejo repository that auto-deploys via strict GitOps webhooks.
options.tradeoffs: High initial architectural complexity to set up the CI/CD pipelines; rigid deployment process that requires strict schema adherence.

options.title: Agent-Driven Infrastructure Lifecycle
options.description: Design the repositories as active workspaces where agents (like BOLT and SYSTEMS) autonomously monitor, update, and self-heal the home lab by generating pull requests for infrastructure updates.
options.tradeoffs: Risk of infinite agent loops or unintended infrastructure mutations if constitutional constraints and validation gates fail.

options.title: The Immutable Memory & State Vault
options.description: Utilize Git repositories not just for code, but as a versioned, time-traveling database for the home lab's state, logs, and KEEPER's memory spine.
options.tradeoffs: Potential for massive repository bloat over time; requires aggressive Git LFS implementation and strict Time-To-Live (TTL) pruning.

options.title: The 'Creator's Fortress' Media Pipeline
options.description: Establish a suite of repositories dedicated entirely to orchestrating the creative liberation engine—automating video rendering, 3D asset generation, and broadcast routing directly on the NAS GPUs.
options.tradeoffs: Highly specialized and resource-intensive; might fragment core infrastructure management from creative infrastructure management.

options.title: Component-First LLM Orchestration
options.description: A repository structure that treats LLMs purely as interchangeable components (Article XXIII), managing their weights, LoRAs, and API adapters locally on the NAS to ensure zero cloud dependency.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant NAS storage for local models; high bandwidth utilization for syncing weights; continuous updates needed.

options.title: The Absolute Thin-Client Paradigm
options.description: A repository structure designed solely to enforce the NAS Supremacy Rule, holding zero local state and turning any connected machine into a dumb terminal via SSH-only execution.
options.tradeoffs: Zero offline capability; absolute dependency on local network stability; high friction for traditional local-first development habits.

options.title: Workstation-Led Repository Syncing
options.description: Managing the home lab by cloning infrastructure repositories to the local workstation (D:\ drive), executing changes locally, and pushing back to the NAS.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates the NAS Supremacy Rule; creates local state dependency; fundamentally breaks the sovereign thin-client architecture.
